key_points.point: Net income fell 51% from $3,314.6M to $1,635.3M (diluted EPS $6.55 to $3.28; net margin 26.9% to 17.3%) on a 23% revenue decline from $12,305.5M to $9,427.2M

Revenue fell mainly because of weaker macroeconomic trends: Industrial down 35% as customers cut their inventory balances, Communications down 33% on the timing of infrastructure deployment cycles, and Automotive (-2%) and Consumer (-1%) down less on weaker consumer spending
Gross margin fell 690 bps to 57.1% from 64.0% (gross margin dollars down $2,495.9M, -32%) because of lower factory utilization from weaker demand and an unfavorable product mix

Lower operating expenses partly offset the decline: SMG&A down $204.9M, amortization down $204.8M (intangibles fully amortized in FY2023), R&D down $172.3M (lower variable compensation) and special charges down $123.5M, even with an extra week in FY2024. Operating income still fell $1,790.3M (-47%) to $2,032.8M
Nonoperating expense rose $40.3M to $255.5M (higher interest expense on debt and lower gains on investments, partly offset by higher interest income), which added to the decline

A $151.4M lower income tax provision ($142.1M vs $293.4M; effective rate about 8% because pretax income was mostly earned in Ireland at 12.5%) partly offset the decline. Note that FY2023 had included an $81.7M discrete tax benefit
Customers' inventory behavior: in the Industrial end market, customers reduced their inventory balances. This was a main driver of Industrial's 35% revenue drop and of the 23% fall in total revenue
The Industrial decline also lowered the distributor channel's share of revenue (58% vs 61%). Distributors buy products to resell them
Lower factory utilization from weaker customer demand, together with unfavorable mix, cut gross margin by 690 bps to 57.1% from 64.0%

The company's own inventory fell 12% to $1,447.7M from $1,642.2M because it worked to balance manufacturing production, demand and inventory levels. Inventory levels depend on forecasted demand and on how far actual demand differs from it
Days cost of sales in inventory still rose to 139 from 125 (calculated from average balances). Changes in working capital partly offset the lower operating cash flow

At November 2, 2024 the company had $2.4B of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, about $1.3B of it in the US. These were highly liquid holdings with highly rated counterparties, and management did not expect repatriation restrictions or taxes to have a material adverse effect

Operating cash flow stayed strong at $3,852.5M, and it rose to 41% of revenue from 39% even as revenue fell. It was down from $4,817.6M because of lower net income, partly offset by changes in working capital
Management believes its existing liquidity, future operating cash and available financing will cover operations, capex, R&D and dividends for at least the next twelve months

Cash used in investing fell to $1,104.9M (lower capex) and cash used in financing fell to $1,714.4M from $4,063.8M (lower stock repurchases). Current liabilities fell to $3.0B from $3.2B on lower accrued liabilities and current debt, partly offset by higher income taxes payable

Signs of pressure: revenue fell 23% and net income 51%, operating cash flow dropped about $965M, and interest expense on debt was higher. Days sales outstanding rose to 54 from 48 and days of inventory rose to 139 from 125, although receivables (-9%) and inventory (-12%) both fell in dollars
